In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: wacom: Advertise SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability prior to registration

Input subsystem guidelines require that device capabilities are advertised
before the input device is registered.  The Wacom driver was violating
this by advertising the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability post-registration in
wacom_set_shared_values() (and duplicating it in device-specific setup
cases).

Resolve this by moving the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability setup to
wacom_setup_touch_input_capabilities() for all touch devices that support
it.

For generic touch devices whose capabilities depend on mute switch
usages parsed from a sibling Pen/Pad interface, defer registration
with -EPROBE_DEFER until the sibling has parsed its descriptors and
initialized shared capabilities.

CVE-2026-99494.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99494.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/zcrypt: Fix out-of-bounds ptr advance in cca_query_crypto_facility()

The FQ reply parser code blindly advanced the walk pointer by a length
value read directly from the hardware reply payload without checking
that the advance stayed within the allocated reply buffer. A corrupt
or malicious device response could push ptr beyond the cprbmem region,
causing an out-of-bounds dereference or kernel memory exposure via the
subsequent memcpy().

Fix this by tracking the remaining reply buffer space in a variable
and validating each device-supplied length field against it before
advancing or dereferencing the pointer.

CVE-2026-99495.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99495.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/zcrypt: Fix and improve zcrypt reply message verification checks

Add or improve checks related to buffer sizes and reply sizes to the
handling of replies from the crypto cards for CCA, EP11 (AP message
type 6) and ICA (AP type 50) messages. The verification code related
to reply field length was not designed well and thus firmware
deficiencies could lead to unexpected behavior in the zcrypt device
driver. Thus improve the code to more closely inspect especially
length fields at message replies.

Add length validation before accessing reply message structures in
zcrypt_msgtype6_receive(), zcrypt_msgtype6_receive_ep11(), and
zcrypt_msgtype50_receive() to prevent out-of-bounds reads and
potential kernel memory disclosure.

Also rework these three functions to validate reply lengths more
carefully before copying data back into the request buffer. Use size_t
for length calculations, reject inconsistent reply sizes, and add
defensive handling for short invalid replies. For XCRB replies,
validate both reply segments and derive the effective message length
from the covered range instead of trusting only the second segment.

Additionally improve some of the later invoked evaluation functions
which further check the payload. Add comments about length assumptions
and for the type50 processing rework the payload processing completely
with removing a misplaced BUG_ON().

CVE-2026-99506.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99506.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio

For a fault in a private mapping with nothing in the page cache,
hugetlb_no_page() allocates a folio, locks it and maps it.  The folio has
one reference, which belongs to the page table entry from then on.  After
dropping the page table lock the function still sets the migratable flag
of the folio and unlocks it.

Whoever zaps the entry in between frees the folio.  The fault holds the
fault mutex and the lock of the vma.  MADV_DONTNEED and the first unmap of
a hole punch, hugetlb_vmdelete_list(), do not take the fault mutex, and a
private vma only has a lock if it owns a reservation map: not with
MAP_NORESERVE, and not in the child after fork().

Then the flag is set in, and folio_unlock() is called on, a folio that is
free or has a new owner.  A surplus page goes back to the page allocator
while it is locked:

  BUG: Bad page state in process init  pfn:108e00
  flags: 0x200000000000059(locked|uptodate|dirty|head|node=0|zone=2)
  page dumped because: PAGE_FLAGS_CHECK_AT_FREE flag(s) set

A page of the pool can be given to the next user, of any file, who locks
it and loses the lock to the late folio_unlock():

  kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:1532!
   hugetlb_no_page+0x111b/0x23e0
   hugetlb_fault+0x3a9/0x14a0

An unprivileged process is enough: threads that write to a MAP_PRIVATE |
MAP_NORESERVE hugetlb mapping, threads that call MADV_DONTNEED on it, and
one that takes the freed pages for another file.

Until commit 3a47c54f09c4 ("hugetlbfs: revert use i_mmap_rwsem for more
pmd sharing synchronization") the fault held i_mmap_rwsem for reading,
which everybody who zaps takes for writing.  The lock that commit
bf4916922c60 ("hugetlbfs: extend hugetlb_vma_lock to private VMAs") gave
to private vmas closed the window again, but only for those with a
reservation map.

Be done with the folio before the page table lock is dropped, as
hugetlb_wp() is with its copy.  The function already unlocks page cache
folios under that lock.

Original fix generated by an LLM and sent in private by Josef.

[david@kernel.org: simplify+move comment]

CVE-2026-99507.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99507.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free in hugetlb_mfill_atomic_pte()

Let's fix another instance where we use a folio after dropping the PTL,
where someone else could e.g., MADV_DONTNEED it once we drop the PTL,
making us trigger a use-after-free on the folio.

CVE-2026-99513.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99513.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked

nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked
under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list
reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window.
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after
the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock
request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops
the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging
off it.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff88811b04c808 by task lockd/8377
    nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230
    nlmsvc_retry_blocked+0x61c/0x800
    lockd+0x144/0x1c0
  Freed by task 8392:
    nlmsvc_release_block+0x231/0x290
    nlmsvc_traverse_blocks+0x139/0x1b0
    nlm_traverse_files+0x1aa/0xa00
    nlmsvc_free_host_resources+0x12/0x60
    nlm_shutdown_hosts_net+0x127/0x280
    lockd_down+0xd5/0x1c0

Take a reference before releasing nlm_blocked_lock and drop it once
the retry has run.

CVE-2026-99514.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99514.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

landlock: Fix superblock use-after-free in release_inode()

Without this fix, release_inode() (task 1) can race with a umount
operation in hook_sb_delete() (task 2).  The order of operations in
which the race occurs is:

* task 2: hook_sb_delete() arrives at the end of the function, waiting
  for landlock_superblock(sb)->inode_refs to become zero.
* task 1: release_inode(): does atomic_long_dec_and_test(), decrementing
  inode_refs to zero.
* task 2: gets woken up through some other means, sees that inode_refs
  is zero and returns.  The caller is the unmount operation and proceeds
  to release the superblock.
* task 1: Runs wake_up_var(&landlock_superblock(sb)->inode_refs),
  *dereferencing the sb_security on the freed-up superblock*.

Notably, wake_up_var() does not dereference the pointer passed to it,
and only uses it to determine an overapproximated set of tasks to wake
up. So while it's potentially possible for an attacker to provide a
different value for that pointer, this only results in the wrong set of
tasks getting woken up, and in this scenario, no further tasks are
actually waiting.

Nevertheless, KASAN detects it as a slab-use-after-free read on
sb->s_security:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in release_inode+0x196/0x290
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff888103b6c0a8 by task repro/217
   release_inode+0x196/0x290
   landlock_put_object+0x71/0x90
   landlock_free_rules+0x38/0xc0
   landlock_put_ruleset+0x47/0x130
   fop_ruleset_release+0x33/0x40
   __fput+0x305/0x780
  Freed by task 54:
   kfree+0x11c/0x390
   process_scheduled_works+0x766/0xe50
   worker_thread+0x7bc/0xb20

The fix is to determine &landlock_superblock(inode->i_sb)->inode_refs only once
earlier in release_inode(), and later use that precalculated address for the
wake_up_var() call, without having to dereference through the superblock.

CVE-2026-99515.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99515.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free

iommufd_eventq_fops_release() drops the file's users reference before
reading eventq->ictx. Once that reference is dropped, IOMMU_DESTROY in
another thread can remove and free the event queue, so the later load
accesses freed memory.

Read ictx while the users reference still pins the event queue, then
drop the reference and put the saved context. The context reference
taken by iommufd_eventq_init() keeps ictx valid until the put. Fault and
vEVENTQ file descriptors share this release path.

CVE-2026-99516.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99516.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet-fc: fix use-after-free in nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection()

nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection() looks up the association with
nvmet_fc_find_target_assoc(), which returns it with a reference held,
and drops that reference as soon as the target queue has been allocated.
iod->assoc is then dereferenced again by nvmet_fc_makeconnid() while
building the connection id.

The queue only borrows the pointer and takes no reference of its own.
Once the lookup reference is dropped the association is kept alive
solely by the reference taken when it was created, so a disconnect LS or
a remote port unregister running concurrently can free it before
nvmet_fc_makeconnid() reads it:

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work (drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:193 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1841 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1995 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:2021)
Read of size 8 at addr ffff888179f1b000 by task kworker/u9:2/1167

Hardware name: QEMU Ubuntu 24.04 PC v2 (i440FX + PIIX, arch_caps fix, 1996), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014
Workqueue: nvmet-wq nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work
Call Trace:

The buggy address belongs to the object at ffff888179f1b000
 which belongs to the cache kmalloc-2k of size 2048
The buggy address is located 0 bytes inside of

on the error path as well.

CVE-2026-99517.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99517.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: fix use-after-free of the old registrant in nvmet_pr_preempt()

nvmet_pr_preempt() handles a preempt sent by the reservation holder by
changing the reservation type with nvmet_pr_update_reg_attr(), unless
the reservation is of an All Registrants type.  For the holder that
helper does not modify the registrant in place: it puts a copy on the
registrant list, points pr->holder to the copy and passes the old
registrant to kfree_rcu().

If the reservation type changed, nvmet_pr_preempt() then hands
&reg->hostid of that old registrant to nvmet_pr_resv_released().  Unless
the reservation released notification is masked, that function takes
subsys->lock and compares the host id against every controller of the
subsystem.  The caller only holds pr->pr_sem and is not in an RCU
read-side critical section, so nothing keeps the old registrant alive
while it is read.

The result is a read of 16 freed bytes that decides which controllers
get the notification.  Found by code inspection.  kfree_rcu() defers
the free, so it usually happens after the read; when the pending free
is forced to run before the read, KASAN reports the host id as freed
memory.

Pass the host id of the controller that sent the command instead.  The
registrant was looked up by that host id, and the controller outlives
the request.

CVE-2026-99522.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99522.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/irdma: avoid use-after-free in icrdma_remove

icrdma_remove() dereferences iwdev after calling
irdma_ib_unregister_device():

  irdma_ib_unregister_device(iwdev)
    -> ib_unregister_device(&iwdev->ibdev)
      -> __ib_unregister_device()
        -> ib_dealloc_device()

irdma registers irdma_ib_dealloc_device() as the dealloc_driver
callback in its ib_device_ops. The RDMA core explicitly documents
ib_unregister_device() that when ops.dealloc_driver is used, ib_dev
will be freed upon return from the function.

The ib_device is embedded in struct irdma_device and iwdev itself was
allocated by ib_alloc_device(irdma_device, ibdev). Consequently, once
irdma_ib_unregister_device() returns, iwdev must no longer be
dereferenced.

However, icrdma_remove() currently accesses iwdev->rf afterwards when
deinitializing interrupts, destroying ah_tbl_lock, and freeing rf.
Although the final ib_device storage is released with kfree_rcu(), the
object lifetime has already ended and callers must not rely on the RCU
grace period to continue dereferencing iwdev.

Save iwdev->rf before unregistering the RDMA device and use the saved
pointer for the remaining cleanup.

This issue was found by manual code inspection.

CVE-2026-99525.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99525.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix use-after-free in cifs_ses_add_channel()

The error path of cifs_ses_add_channel() calls cifs_put_tcp_session()
before cifs_chan_clear_need_reconnect().  The latter reaches
cifs_ses_get_chan_index(), which dereferences server->terminate; if
the put was the final reference, TCP_Server_Info is already freed and
this is a use-after-free.  Same put-then-use pattern as the recently
fixed sibling in commit 717e0a25036b ("cifs: Fix server use-after-free
in cifs_chan_skip_or_disable()").

Move the put last, but do not read chan->server after dropping
chan_lock: chan points into ses->chans[], and once chan_count is
decremented a concurrent add_channel can reuse the slot and overwrite
the pointer, so the put would act on the new channel's server.  Cache
the pointer under chan_lock, clear the reconnect bit and decrement
chan_count while still holding the reference, and release it after
the unlock.

This issue was discovered by Tencent CodeBuddy Security.

CVE-2026-99526.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99526.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix use-after-free infoleak via the readdir resume name

CIFSFindNext() copies the resume name that cifs_save_resume_key()
recorded from the last entry of the previous response into its request;
psrch_inf->presume_name points into the response buffer that entry came
from, and nothing ever clears it. find_cifs_entry() records a new
name only from a response with a usable last entry, and cifs_readdir()
only from an entry it walks to, so a response that carries no entries
and leaves last_entry NULL, because CIFSFindFirst() or CIFSFindNext()
rejected LastNameOffset, refreshes neither and presume_name keeps
pointing into the previous response. That buffer has already been
released: by CIFSFindNext() before it installs the new response, or by
find_cifs_entry() when it rewinds the search, which does not drop the
name either and can then fail in initiate_cifs_search() before a new
response replaces it. The next CIFSFindNext() then copies up to
PATH_MAX - 1 bytes of the resume name out of the released buffer into
its request and sends them to the server: a use-after-free read
that leaks kernel memory to a malicious or compromised server, which
can provoke it with a single FindNext response that carries no entries
and a LastNameOffset above CIFSMaxBufSize, which is all the existing
check rejects.

With KASAN enabled, a server that answers a listing that way gives:

 CIFS: VFS: ignoring corrupt resume name
 ==================================================================
 BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0
 Read of size 4080 at addr ffff88807c823f98 by task ls/83

 CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 83 Comm: ls Tainted: G    B               7.3.0-rc4-00457-gf14572c203d5 #69 PREEMPT(lazy)
 Tainted: [B]=BAD_PAGE
 Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  kasan_report+0xdf/0x1a0
  kasan_check_range+0x10f/0x1e0
  __asan_memcpy+0x23/0x60
  CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0
  cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0
  iterate_dir+0x1c0/0x570
  __x64_sys_getdents64+0x133/0x270
  do_syscall_64+0x109/0x5d0
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
  </TASK>

 Allocated by task 83 on cpu 1 at 13.497119s:
  cifs_buf_get+0x36/0x90
  smb_init+0x4f/0x110
  CIFSFindNext+0xf7/0x14c0
  cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0

 Freed by task 83 on cpu 0 at 13.584018s:
  cifs_buf_release+0x41/0x80
  CIFSFindNext+0xfce/0x14c0
  cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0

 The buggy address is located 16280 bytes inside of
  freed 16588-byte region [ffff88807c820000, ffff88807c8240cc)
 ==================================================================

The same memcpy() first reads past the end of that object while it is
still live, a slab-out-of-bounds read that the following patches
bound; that is the taint the report above carries.

SMB1 is not negotiated by default; reaching this code requires an
explicit vers=1.0 mount.

Clear presume_name and resume_name_len whenever a new response is
installed and when the rewind path releases the search buffer, so that
the name never outlives the buffer it points into, and reset
resume_key with them, since it was taken from the same entry and would
otherwise be sent with an empty name. A response without a usable
last entry then continues the search with an empty resume name rather
than a stale one; CIFSFindNext() skips the copy of a zero-length name
so that it never runs on the NULL pointer.

The next patch in the series leaves last_entry NULL for a response
that carries no entries, and bounds LastNameOffset against the
received response rather than against CIFSMaxBufSize. Responses that
are given a last entry today then take the path fixed here, so that
patch must not be applied without this one.

CVE-2026-99528.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99528.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp()

While fuzzing with a customized syzkaller, I hit a refcount warning in
xprt_alloc(), reached from a write to /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy:

  refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free.
  WARNING: lib/refcount.c:25 at refcount_warn_saturate+0xf8/0x120
  CPU: 0 PID: 10404 Comm: syz.0.17 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1-00096-gcfebfd3db73d
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   xprt_alloc+0x83f/0x9d0
   xs_setup_xprt+0xaf/0x3c0
   xs_setup_local+0x47/0x7f0
   xprt_create_transport+0x16c/0x730
   rpc_create+0x38e/0x7f0
   gssp_rpc_create+0xe2/0x180
   set_gssp_clnt+0xba/0x1b0
   write_gssp+0x200/0x310
   proc_reg_write+0x240/0x330
   vfs_write+0x2aa/0x1050
   ksys_write+0x12a/0x250
   do_syscall_64+0x117/0x750
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
   </TASK>

create_use_gss_proxy_proc_entry() stores the struct net pointer as the
proc entry's private data without taking a reference on it, and an open
file descriptor does not pin the namespace either, as procfs only pins
the proc_dir_entry. write_gssp() reads that pointer back with
pde_data() and hands it to set_gssp_clnt(), which reaches xprt_init():

	xprt->xprt_net = get_net_track(net, &xprt->ns_tracker, GFP_KERNEL);

get_net_track() -> get_net() -> refcount_inc() is unconditional, so
rpc_create() assumes its caller holds a reference on args.net.
write_gssp() does not.

Dropping the last ns.count reference does not make the file go away.
__put_net() only queues cleanup_net() on a workqueue, and the
remove_proc_entry() that fences off further writes runs from the
rpcsec_gss pernet .exit method, that is, from inside cleanup_net(). A
write landing between those two points increments a refcount that is
already zero. cleanup_net() does not re-read ns.count, so the namespace
is freed anyway and the rpc_xprt -- along with the AF_LOCAL socket
opened for it -- is left pointing at freed memory. The resurrected
count is visible to the rest of that teardown too: with
CONFIG_IPV6_MROUTE the same cleanup_net() worker then trips
!mr_can_free_table() in ip6mr_free_table(), which tests check_net() on
the namespace it is freeing.

It reduces to opening /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy inside a new network
namespace, calling setns() back to the original one to drop the last
reference, and then writing "1" to the still-open descriptor.

Take the reference in write_gssp() itself and refuse the write when the
namespace is already gone. This is what procfs does for every other
/proc/net file: get_proc_net() is maybe_get_net(PDE_NET(PDE(inode)))
and seq_open_net() returns -ENXIO when it fails. PDE_NET() cannot be
reused here because the parent directory /proc/net/rpc carries no
namespace pointer. Adding a .pre_exit to rpcsec_gss_net_ops so the
entry is removed earlier would only narrow the window, since pre_exit
also runs from cleanup_net().

Live namespaces are unaffected: a write still returns the error from
set_gssp_clnt(), a write of "2" still returns -EINVAL, and reads are
untouched.

CVE-2026-99544.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99544.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices

In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and
write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as
potentially malicious.

hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds
checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset
up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too:
the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how
much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than
the ring.

The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated
snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices,
hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO.

One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch:
hv_get_ring_bufferindices() fetches it again for the prev_indices
trailer. The value is only returned to the host and is not used as an
offset or length for indexing. Since this is not a security issue, it is
addressed later in the series.

Open-coding the bytes available arithmetic keeps the fix free of
prerequisites; a later patch refactors it into a helper function.

CVE-2026-99545.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99545.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

driver core: take parent lock on deferred probe

USB interfaces should be probed with the parent USB device lock held,
but this is not honoured when probe is deferred.

Add a new bus_probe_device_deferred() helper to handle deferred probe
where the parent device lock is not held.

CVE-2026-99546.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99546.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete

Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the
classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or
hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then
dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.

Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero.
Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller
still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to
free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still
holds the filter.

The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately.
Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty
mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to
determine whether the classifier has become empty.

Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed
pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common
failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference.

This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

CVE-2026-99547.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99547.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug

When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch
subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its
child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an
attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM
completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not
guaranteed numerically sorted).

I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would
seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I
tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if
that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found
that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault
at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went
bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I
ultimately ended up changing. To confirm this issue, I did an eBPF trace
of `bus_for_each_dev()`, `complete_rpm()`, and `complete()` while
unplugging in a variety of situations and found that an unplug from
domain 0 tries to `complete_rpm()` domain 1's switch, whose RPM
completion is not initialized and thus is holding a null wait-list
pointer, triggering the page fault.

Here are the key sections of that eBPF trace. Note that HEAD denotes the
completion's own wait-list HEAD:

```
RESCAN_ENTER domain=0

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=0-1 target_domain=0
         route=0x1 parent=0-0 unplugged=1
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=HEAD prev=HEAD

BUS_WALK domain=0 start=0-1 callback=complete_rpm
CALLBACK_ENTER rescan_domain=0 dev=1-0 parent=domain1 is_switch=1

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=1-0 target_domain=1
         route=0x0 parent=domain1 unplugged=0
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=0 prev=0

        complete+5
        complete_rpm+43
        bus_for_each_dev+133
        icm_free_unplugged_children+250
        icm_rescan_work+42
```

This patch gates the `complete()` on an additional condition - that the
Thunderbolt domain matches the domain of the device that was unplugged.

I only have a single system with multiple Thunderbolt domains - the Dell
XPS9720. I am consistently able to reproduce the Oops on that system.
Since running with this patch, I have not seen the Oops reoccur. I have
also tested it on a Thinkpad X1-Gen12, and that system boots and runs
well with it, but it only has a single Thunderbolt domain, so it does
not exercise the multi-domain failure case.

CVE-2026-99548.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99548.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race

Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of
the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily
uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this
empty procfs, iterating over a zeroed list_head leads to a NULL
pointer dereference and a kernel oops/panic.

For example, if a delay is added between cifs_proc_init() and
INIT_LIST_HEAD, and a userspace process is polling
/proc/fs/cifs/DebugData, the following oops occurs:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000608
Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 3477 Comm: cat Not tainted
7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:cifs_debug_data_proc_show+0x103/0xd80 [cifs]
Call Trace:
<TASK>
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 seq_read_iter+0x183/0x400
 proc_reg_read_iter+0x62/0x90
 copy_splice_read+0x215/0x310
 splice_file_to_pipe+0xec/0x1c0
 do_splice+0x4b8/0x780
 __se_sys_splice+0x18f/0x250
 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x330
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
</TASK>

Fix this by moving cifs_proc_init() down in init_cifs(), ensuring it runs
only after all internal lists, locks, counters, and workqueues are fully
ready, but before registering the filesystem. Update the error cleanup
ladder and exit_cifs() to maintain proper LIFO order.

CVE-2026-99549.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99549.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_break()

receive_encrypted_read() sets *num_mids = 1 and never writes the
caller's bufs[]. Offload returns -1 with *num_mids = 0, so the
demultiplex thread skips the frame. The inline decrypt path
returns 0 even when smb2_find_mid() fails.

cifs_demultiplex_thread() then treats mids[i] == NULL as an
oplock break and calls is_oplock_break(bufs[i], server) with
bufs[i] still NULL. smb2_is_valid_oplock_break() reads
hdr.Command at offset 12 and oopses.

A large encrypted READ whose MessageId does not match is enough
to panic cifsd.

    Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
    0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
    KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range
    [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f]
    CPU: 0 PID: 100 Comm: cifsd
    RIP: smb2_is_valid_oplock_break+0xc8/0x2270 [cifs]
    cifs_demultiplex_thread
    Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Return -1 when inline decrypt finds no mid, and skip
is_oplock_break() plus the unknown-frame dump when bufs[i]
is NULL. receive_encrypted_standard() already assigns
bufs[*num_mids].

CVE-2026-99554.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99554.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: usb: pegasus: do not advance rx_skb->data on dropped frames

For the 0x8513 chip, read_bulk_callback() skips the 2-byte receive
header by advancing pegasus->rx_skb->data in place. This is done before
the pkt_len > PEGASUS_MTU check, and when that check drops the frame
the good path resubmits the same skb with the advanced rx_skb->data as
the transfer buffer, still PEGASUS_MTU bytes long.

Every frame with an oversized length field therefore moves the receive
buffer two more bytes towards the end of the skb data area. A device
that keeps sending such frames makes the host controller write received
data over skb_shared_info and past the end of the allocation, and the
corrupted skb_shared_info is used when the skb is eventually freed.
With an emulated device sending frames filled with 0x5a on a KASAN
kernel:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in dummy_timer+0xade/0x3f00 [dummy_hcd]
  Write of size 1536 at addr ffff888105821202 by task swapper/1/0
  ...
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xeb4b474b4b4b4b4c: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP KASAN NOPTI
  KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access in range [0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a60-0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a67]
  RIP: 0010:skb_release_data+0x36f/0x800

Only skip the header with skb_reserve() once the frame is going to be
passed up, so the receive buffer always starts at the beginning of the
skb data area. Unlike the old pointer adjustment, skb_reserve() also
moves skb->tail, so the two header bytes now count against the buffer
size: lower the length limit for the 0x8513 accordingly, otherwise a
pkt_len of PEGASUS_MTU - 1 or PEGASUS_MTU would trip skb_over_panic().

Found by code review with LLM assistance and reproduced with an
emulated USB device (raw-gadget + dummy_hcd).

CVE-2026-99557.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99557.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR
request with a reply whose extra blob is empty.  parse_reply_info()
skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir()
never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still
parses as successful.  ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and
ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check:

	/* extra */
	ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad);
	if (len > 0) {
		...
		err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s);
		...
	}

The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the
mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed:

BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10
 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0
 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0
 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0
 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>

The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle
frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old.

Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once,
drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already
handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function.

Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN).  Unpatched, the
getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first
READDIR reply.  With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2)
returns -EIO, no oops, no hang.  A conformant reply for an empty
directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE —
still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal
readdir behavior is unchanged.  The oops is still present in
v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45).

CVE-2026-99561.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99561.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set

zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set.
Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't
catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and
it isn't sent SIGKILL.

do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls
io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task
work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates
a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in
the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being
dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it
exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and
decrements threads_remaining like any other thread.

So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves
coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running.

The task has no fatal signal pending because zap_process() deliberately
didn't send it one, and it never went through get_signal() so it doesn't
have PF_SIGNALED either.

Refuse to create an io thread when the creator has PF_POSTCOREDUMP.
That costs nothing. io_uring_files_cancel() raises IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
before it runs any task work, so a worker created from there only ever
gets to exit again, and io_should_retry_thread() doesn't retry -EINTR.

Clearing PF_POSTCOREDUMP for the new thread in copy_process() was the
other option. It makes the worker a thread like any other, but it only
helps while the dump hasn't started. A worker born after zap_process()
has run is invisible to it whatever its flags say and still decrements
threads_remaining on the way out. Refusing to create it covers both, and
then no task is ever born with the flag, so there is nothing to clear.

Moving io_uring_files_cancel() ahead of synchronize_group_exit() closes
the same window. It runs the cancellation, and whatever that can block
on, before the thread announces itself to the dumper. A thread that
blocks there never reaches coredump_task_exit() at all, so the dumper
ends up waiting for a thread that never parks. Refusing the creation
leaves the cancellation where it is. But it's very ugly to run io_uring
work even before we did all the generic exit work.

CVE-2026-99566.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99566.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

assoc_array: keep gc's cleanup out of the live tree on allocation failure

assoc_array_gc() builds a copy of the tree.  Where the copy reaches a
shortcut, it allocates the copy of the shortcut with kmalloc_flex(),
fills it with memcpy(), links it into the new tree, and only then
allocates the copy of the node after it.  The memcpy() leaves the new
shortcut's next_node pointing at the old tree's node, so if that second
allocation fails, the cleanup, assoc_array_destroy_subtree() on the new
tree, follows the new shortcut into the old tree, and the BUG_ON() on
the old node's back pointer fires.

Allocate the node first, and the shortcut once the node exists, freeing
the node again if the shortcut cannot be allocated.  A copied shortcut
is then only linked into the new tree when the copy of its node is there
to follow it.  Nothing else changes: with no allocation failing, the
trees gc builds are the same as before.

Found by a userspace test that makes each allocation of each operation
fail in turn.

CVE-2026-99567.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99567.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

assoc_array: don't chain a new shortcut onto an existing one

When a full node's leaves and the new key all share the node's segment,
assoc_array_insert_into_terminal_node() replaces the node with a
shortcut to a pair of new nodes.  If the node is itself the target of a
shortcut, the new shortcut is installed as that shortcut's next node,
and a shortcut leading to a shortcut is something nothing expects:
assoc_array_walk() indexes the second one as a node, and
assoc_array_apply_edit() hits the BUG_ON() in the loop that adjusts
nr_leaves_on_branch, on that same insertion.

Deletion gets a node there.  When the subtree below a shortcut shrinks
enough, assoc_array_delete() collapses it into one node below the
shortcut, and the leaves it collects can all share that node's segment.
The next key that shares it too takes this path.  Eighteen insertions
and a deletion are enough: sixteen keys that agree on bits 0-11, one
that leaves them at bit 8 and is deleted again, and one more that agrees
with the sixteen.

Have the new shortcut replace the one in front of the node as well.
assoc_array_insert_shortcut() gives it that shortcut's back pointer and
parent slot, so the caller installs it where that one was, and excises
the old shortcut along with the node, which takes a second entry in
excised_meta[].  The new shortcut's index key comes from the new key up
to the new skip level, so it covers what the old one did.

Found by a userspace test doing random insertions and deletions on keys
that share long prefixes; a targeted case builds a shortcut, deletes
down to the collapse and inserts one more key.

CVE-2026-99568.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99568.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommufd/iova_bitmap: Ensure that iova_bitmap_set() handles the full IOVA

Generally userspace is going to step the dirty bitmap through the IOVA
space. However if the bitmap ends in the middle of a large PTE this is
problematic. The first step will clear the dirty bit and report dirty to
the end of its bitmap while the second step will see the clear'd dirty and
report clean for the start of the bitmap. If it happens this ends up
losing dirties.

Further this function is missing bounds checking so if this does happen
ther is a good chance it will write memory beyond what the userspace was
expecting.

Return an error code if this illegal condition happens.

CVE-2026-99571.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99571.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme-tcp: Validate the queue state under the queue lock in the address attribute

Reading the "address" sysfs attribute calls kernel_getsockname() on the
admin queue socket, which can race with the queue teardown during
connection error recovery: a reader can observe NVME_TCP_Q_LIVE set,
then block on the queue lock while nvme_tcp_free_queue() releases the
socket and clears queue->sock without holding the lock.  Once the
reader acquires the lock it dereferences the NULL socket pointer.

Commit 76d54bf20cdc ("nvme-tcp: don't access released socket during
error recovery") had the queue liveness check inside the lock.
Commit 782373ba2766 ("nvme: tcp: avoid race between queue_lock lock
and destroy") moved it back out because the lock itself is destroyed
in nvme_tcp_free_queue(), so a reader arriving late trips
mutex_destroy().

Check the queue liveness inside the queue lock, and clear queue->sock
under the same lock.  The teardown clears NVME_TCP_Q_LIVE under the
lock well before the socket is released, so a reader either sees the
bit cleared or a socket that cannot be released while it holds the
lock.  To also close the lock lifetime race, the queue locks are now
owned by the controller: they are initialized with the queue array and
only destroyed when the controller is freed, which cannot happen while
a sysfs attribute read is still in progress.  The queue count is
computed by the NVME_TCP_OPT_NR_QUEUES() macro from the original
connect options for both initialization and destruction, as reconnects
may shrink ctrl->queue_count.

CVE-2026-99573.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99573.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: arm64: vgic: Stop the target vcpu when disabling LPIs

Disabling LPIs is pretty nasty, as it directly messes with the AP list
of the affected CPU, which could be running... This has the potential to
lead to really bad behaviours, and we should not be doing that.

Take example on the way the Active state is handled and simply pause the
the vcpu so that we are sure it is in a quiescent state, and the state be
safely manipulated.

Nobody has any expectation of performance for this anyway.

CVE-2026-99577.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99577.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: rtw88: usb: bound what the driver feeds the after-DTIM queue

Frames routed to the high queue are transmitted right after DTIM beacons
only, inside the ATIM window, while they wait in the shared TX page pool.
The driver puts no limit on how many it hands over, so as long as one
station dozes, any sustained broadcast or multicast traffic outruns the
drain and empties the pool: measured on an RTL8822BU AP with a single
client in power save and ~40 frames/s of mDNS chatter, the free page
count at 0x240 goes from 1803 to 16 in about 100 seconds and stays there
for as long as the traffic lasts. From that point every other transmit
queues behind the backlog, authentication responses arrive too late for
anyone to join, and the reserved page download fails ("error beacon
valid"). The AP keeps beaconing and only a reboot recovers.

Feed the high queue through a small budget that refills below the
measured drain rate (about 3 frames per DTIM, ~15/s at dtim_period 2 on
the default 2 TU ATIM window); whatever exceeds the budget leaves on its
access category queue right away. The high queue backlog is now bounded
by the burst size under any load, so the page pool cannot run dry, at
the price that a dozing station may miss part of a broadcast storm.

CVE-2026-99578.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99578.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: rtw88: usb: route bmc frames via the high queue only for DTIM delivery

In AP mode every broadcast and multicast data frame is routed to
TX_DESC_QSEL_HIGH, the after-DTIM queue, whether or not anybody is
asleep. The firmware drains that queue at beacon pace, a dozen or so
frames per second measured on RTL8822BU, while one associated client's
mDNS/SSDP chatter alone exceeds that. The excess accumulates inside
the chip until the shared TX page pool is exhausted (measured: 14 of
1803 pages left). From that point every host-sourced frame queues
behind the backlog: authentication responses reach the air seconds
after the client has given up, so no station can associate anymore,
and the beacon reserved-page download fails the BCN_VALID poll
("error beacon valid") because it needs pages from the same pool. The
AP keeps beaconing, so the failure looks like a silent RX stall and
only a reboot recovers.

mac80211 already decides when after-DTIM delivery is needed: it sets
IEEE80211_TX_CTL_SEND_AFTER_DTIM on bmc frames only while at least one
station is actually dozing. Honor that instead of routing
unconditionally: flagged frames keep going through the high queue with
the MORE_DATA and HGQMD handling introduced by commit 076f786a0ae1
("wifi: rtw88: Fix AP mode incorrect DTIM behavior"), everything else
leaves at line rate through the AC queues. This partially reverts the
usb.c hunk of that commit, whose unconditional routing is what lets
the backlog build up.

On a bench AP (USB2, 20 MHz, WPA2, hostapd, a Windows client driven
through disconnect/reconnect cycles): reconnects fail 0/5 on RTL8822BU
and 0/3 on RTL8821CU before this change, and pass 10/10 and 5/5 with
it, with the page pool staying healthy and no beacon errors logged.

CVE-2026-99582.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99582.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: re-point retained control chunks on association migration

sctp_sock_migrate() transfers DATA chunk ownership but leaves retained
control chunks pointing at the old socket. A later retransmission can
therefore access the socket after it has been freed.

Extend the migration walk to cover retained control chunks and use
sctp_control_set_owner_w() to assign their new owner. Reuse the DATA
ownership check so each chunk is processed once per pass, even when it
is reachable through multiple lists or retained pointers.

Preserve a control chunk's existing authentication key across migration
so its final release can still generate SCTP_AUTH_FREE_KEY when needed.

CVE-2026-99583.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99583.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: hold shkey across socket migration

sctp_sock_migrate() transfers queued DATA skbs from the old socket to the
new one. skb_orphan() invokes sctp_wfree() during that transfer and drops
the skb-owned shared-key reference.

If userspace has removed that key from the association, this can be the
final reference. The following sctp_set_owner_w() then dereferences the
freed chunk->shkey while trying to take the new owner reference.

Take a temporary shared-key reference before orphaning the skb and release
it after the new owner has taken its reference. This preserves the selected
authentication key throughout the ownership transfer.

Bug found and triaged by OpenAI Security Research and
validated by Trail of Bits.

CVE-2026-99586.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99586.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Handle ARM erratum for CONT under invalidation with SVA

The erratum (MMU-700: #3777127, S3: #3673557) deals with under
invalidation of a CONT PTE grouping in the SMMU. The recommended work
around is to use a range invalidation that spans the entire CONT. The only
user of CONT in the kernel right now is through SVA sharing a CPU page
table that contains a CONT created by the mm.

Previously it was thought that this errata was dealt with because the
driver always uses range invalidation. However, there is a subtle detail
in the errata that the invalidation range must fully enclose the entire
CONT for it to work.

It seems that two sequential range invalidations, with a split point
falling inside a CONT grouping, will not prevent the errata.

The SMMU's range invalidation generation algorithm does not produce a
single invalidation for a single SVA invalidation request, nor does the mm
carefully align the SVA invalidation ranges to accommodate the splitting
of the invalidation into several ranges.

Thus, when processing a SVA invalidation, the range invalidation splitting
routine can generate a range invalidation that is split in the middle of
the CONT and risk under invalidation from this errata. This condition
could be triggered by a malicious userspace manipulating the TLB gathers
via mmap/mprotect/munmap.

Update the errata list to the include the S3 variation, detect the IOMMUs
that have it, and then have SVA invalidations use a simplified version of
the over invalidation algorithm from the tlbi rework series. This ensures
that a single range invalidation is issued for a single MMU notifier
callback and now the range invalidation is guarenteed to cover any posible
CONT.

Future work to add CONT to iommu_domain page tables should either use this
one-invalidate/one-range invalidation algorithm or disable CONT support in
the iommu_domain.

CVE-2026-99587.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99587.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ata: libata-scsi: reject data-in commands with a data-out buffer

SG_IO can submit a data-in SCSI command with DMA_TO_DEVICE. The
scatterlist can then contain pages pinned without write access.
ata_scsi_rbuf_fill() writes simulated replies to that scatterlist;
in the reported case, the copy tried to write the shared zero page
and faulted in the kernel.

The same mismatch can affect SG_IO commands translated by libata.
ZBC IN and GET PHYSICAL ELEMENT STATUS completion handlers can modify
the receive buffer even if the drive aborts the command. For ATAPI,
the successful INQUIRY completion also rewrites the buffer in
atapi_fixup_inquiry().

Reject these mismatched commands before the buffer is written or the
command is issued. Report ABORTED COMMAND / DATA IN BUFFER ERROR because
the CDB itself can be valid; the supplied transfer direction is wrong.

CVE-2026-99590.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99590.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data()

The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the
client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need()
only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes.
ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio
with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more
inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end.

Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant()
and fill_inode(), are covered.

CVE-2026-99591.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99591.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size

IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE)
that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table.
For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the
IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the
device table.

The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB
pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the
out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit
this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring
down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device
table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB.

Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected
processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a
(Zen5/BRH).

This is a mitigation for CVE-2024-21963.

kdump reuses the previous kernel's device table only when the size
encoded in the IOMMU device-table register matches
pci_seg->dev_table_size. A mixed rollout disagrees: the unpatched
kernel uses the IVRS-derived size and the patched kernel uses 2MB,
so __reuse_device_table() rejects the table. On SNP-capable IOMMUs
that rejection panics the kdump kernel. Kernels that both have this
patch agree on 2MB and reuse succeeds. Update the production kernel
and the crash kernel together.

CVE-2026-99593.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99593.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

arm64: sdei: Preserve the interrupted context's exception registers

An SDEI event is dispatched by firmware regardless of PSTATE.DAIF, so it
can interrupt the kernel where the exception registers are live:

 - exception entry, before kernel_entry has saved ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and
   before the C handler has read ESR_EL1/FAR_EL1;
 - exception return, after kernel_exit has loaded ELR_EL1/SPSR_EL1 and
   before the ERET.

An IRQ or pseudo-NMI cannot arrive there with PSTATE.I set. Firmware
saves only x0-x17, PC and PSTATE around an SDEI event, so a synchronous
exception taken by the handler overwrites the interrupted context's
ELR, SPSR, ESR and FAR. do_sdei_event() only notices that ELR changed,
and warns.

The interrupted context then carries on with the handler's state. A
task interrupted on its way into the kernel can be sent SIGILL for the
handler's kernel data abort. A task interrupted on its way back to user
space ERETs to EL1, at the handler's fixup address, with user registers
loaded.

With SDEI delivering NMI backtraces, this happens in normal operation.
The handler runs show_regs(), which reads through possibly-NULL pointers
with the _nofault() accessors. print_worker_info() faults this way for a
kworker that is not running a work item, and a single sysrq-l warned
once per such kworker.

Save ELR, SPSR, ESR and FAR in __sdei_handler() before
irqentry_nmi_enter(), which can take an exception too, and restore them
after irqentry_nmi_exit().

Once they are restored, a nested exception is harmless if its handler is
safe in NMI context. That holds for EL1 data aborts on translation,
permission and access-flag faults, which never take the mmap lock in NMI
context, and for BRK. Warn once, with the syndrome, about any other
exception class.

CVE-2026-99596.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99596.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme: wait for SRCU readers before splicing the namespace list

Readers walk ctrl->namespaces under ctrl->srcu, and some of them sleep
there, e.g. nvme_wait_freeze() waiting for I/O to drain.

nvme_remove_namespaces() moves the list onto its on-stack ns_list with
list_splice_init_rcu(), which only waits for RCU readers before
relinking the entries. A reader still on the last namespace then follows
its next pointer to ns_list instead of ctrl->namespaces and treats the
stack as a namespace. Deleting a controller while a Format NVM
passthrough waits for a delayed read on the last namespace gives:

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in nvme_wait_freeze+0x102/0x120
  Read of size 8 at addr ff110001d2f3fc38 by task nvme/4413
  Call Trace:
   nvme_wait_freeze
   nvme_passthru_start
   nvme_submit_user_cmd
   nvme_user_cmd
   nvme_dev_ioctl
  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffffff8af04850

Use list_splice_init_srcu() instead, which waits for the SRCU readers.
This also takes the RCU grace period out of every controller deletion.
Deleting 64 tcp controllers with one namespace each, median of 3 runs on
each of two boots per kernel:

                                      before        after
  nvme disconnect-all (ms)            3491 / 3509   2996 / 3165
  nvme_remove_namespaces() avg (ms)   39.0 / 40.5   31.9 / 34.7

CVE-2026-99601.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99601.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded

udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest
to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block
inside the partition.  Nothing checks that.  A zero-length extent makes
it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and
the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type
bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation.  An extent running
past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the
partition.

Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous
commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind
in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents
running past the partition.

Check every extent once when the table is loaded, and refuse
read-write access if one is empty, is not a whole number of blocks, or
does not lie inside the partition, in the same way as for other
allocation information the kernel cannot use.  Check first that the
table is an Unallocated Space Entry at all: the walk starts at the
offset of the allocation descriptors in one, and for a file entry that
offset lies before the inode's in-memory copy of the descriptors.
Treat a chain of allocation extent descriptors that leads back to
itself the same way: the walk would otherwise return the same extents
forever, and the mount would never finish.  Let a fatal signal
interrupt the walk and fail the mount.

Refusing read-write access to an empty extent is deliberate.  It shows
that an old kernel took the last block but left the entry behind.  If
consumed again, the entry returns an in-use block and turns into a huge
bogus extent.  Refusing the table before that
happens avoids this second allocation; the filesystem can still be
mounted read-only.  The check cannot detect every overlap that may
already exist in a damaged table.

This patch should be backported together with the previous one: that
patch stops creating new empty extents, and this one rejects existing
ones before they are consumed again.

CVE-2026-99602.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99602.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent

udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table
extent closest to the goal.  It keeps that extent's type and length
together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only
if goal_elen then reaches zero.  UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the
free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1
(allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way.  For
such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last
block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the
block after the extent, which is in use.

The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use
block.  Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type
bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize:
about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other
table extents and whatever lies behind the partition.  From then on
blocks are handed out twice, or past the end of the partition.

Extents that udf_table_free_blocks() adds are type 0, where the check
works, so only tables written by mkudffs or by another implementation
are affected.  Nothing more than filling such a filesystem is needed:
on a fresh 1 MiB "mkudffs --space=unalloctable" image, creating empty
files until the partition is full writes file entries over the reserve
volume descriptor sequence and the backup anchor, and df then reports a
negative amount of used space.

On syzbot's images the same double allocation is what the two reports
below trip over.  In the first, ftruncate() extends a new file with
enough hole extents to need a chain of allocation extent descriptors;
one AED is placed on another inode's file entry, and a later one is
placed on the block of the AED currently being filled, which
udf_setup_indirect_aext() zeroes, so __udf_add_aext() finds
lengthAllocDescs out of step with its cursor.  In the second, an AED
is placed past the end of the device, sb_getblk() fails, and the error
path of udf_do_extend_file() calls udf_truncate_extents() on an extent
list that no longer covers i_size.

Keep the type separately from the length, as udf_table_prealloc_blocks()
already does.

CVE-2026-99606.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99606.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/smc: don't spin in smc_rx_recvmsg() while a pipe holds spliced data

While bytes spliced off the RMB are still in a pipe, recvmsg() waits
for the pipe to release them before it copies the data behind them.
The path to that wait skips the timeout and signal checks, and
smc_rx_wait() returns at once on RCV_SHUTDOWN. With a signal pending,
after SHUT_RD, or once the peer closes or shuts down writing,
recvmsg() spins on a CPU until the pipe is drained, and SIGKILL cannot
stop it. MSG_DONTWAIT and an expired SO_RCVTIMEO wait there too
instead of returning -EAGAIN.

Check the timeout and signals before that wait, and end it when the
pipe releases the data or the connection is killed, not on RCV_SHUTDOWN.
A zero-length read returns 0 without waiting for the pipe; a
non-blocking one returns -EAGAIN while poll() still reports the socket
readable (splice() can still take those bytes). The wait sets
SOCKWQ_ASYNC_WAITDATA like smc_rx_wait(), so a byte arriving behind
the pipe raises no SIGIO on a reader already asleep for it, and a full
barrier orders its wait queue entry before its read of splice_pending,
so no wake is lost.

CVE-2026-99611.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99611.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: line6: Reject capture buffers smaller than two packets

line6_capture_copy() splits the copy into the ALSA ring buffer once at
the buffer end and wraps pos_done once, which is only correct when one
packet holds at most buffer_size frames. The packet size comes from the
device's endpoint, and the per-device hw structs allow 64-byte periods
with periods_min 1, so a packet can be larger than the whole buffer.
audio_in_callback() logs an oversized packet and then copies it anyway.

The packet size is known at probe time, so constrain
SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_BUFFER_BYTES in snd_line6_capture_open() to at least
twice the larger of the two endpoints' packet sizes. Two rather than
one, because pos_done advances by the packet and wraps once, so a buffer
of exactly one packet leaves the position unchanged after every packet.
hw_params then rejects a buffer that cannot hold two packets, and the
single wrap is valid for every configuration that gets through. Keep a
guard in line6_capture_copy() that drops an oversized packet with a
ratelimited error, for the case that should no longer be reachable.

Reproduced on 7.3-rc7 with a USB/IP device presenting the GuitarPort
interface layout and 1024-byte packets into a 128-byte buffer: ALSA
logged "invalid position: pos = 224, buffer size = 32" and the driver
logged "driver bug: len" on every following packet. With this patch a
1024-byte buffer is refused at hw_params, and a 2048-byte buffer streams
for 30 s with no report and with the position moving inside the buffer.

CVE-2026-99613.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99613.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: cs46xx: Handle SCB creation failures before dereferencing

With CONFIG_PM_SLEEP enabled, cs46xx_dsp_create_scb() can return NULL
if kmemdup() fails to allocate the SCB data saved for resume.
cs46xx_dsp_scb_and_task_init() and _dsp_create_generic_scb() dereference
the returned pointer without checking it, causing a NULL pointer
dereference on allocation failure.

Check both return values before accessing the SCB descriptors.
Return -ENOMEM when creating the null SCB fails and propagate NULL
from _dsp_create_generic_scb().

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE
static analysis tool.

CVE-2026-99616.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99616.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin

A file opened by file handle on an overlay with nfs_export=on can show
the stale lower data of a file that was copied up to the upper layer.
While the file opened this way stays in the inode cache, a lookup of the
copied up file by path fails with ESTALE for all users. The open can
also succeed for a file that was removed, where it has to fail with
ESTALE. This happens with a handle that has one byte changed. The handle
comes from an NFS client, or from a process that calls
open_by_handle_at() with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH in the initial user
namespace.

When a file in a lower layer is about to be modified, overlayfs first
copies it to the upper layer (copy up). With nfs_export=on, each copy up
also creates an entry in the index directory, a directory that overlayfs
keeps for itself on the upper filesystem.

The handle of an overlay file that comes from a lower layer wraps the
handle of its lower inode. Overlayfs calls this lower inode the origin.
The overlay handle stays valid after a copy up.

To decode such a handle, ovl_lower_fh_to_d() first decodes the wrapped
handle to the origin. If no overlay inode is cached for the origin, it
looks in the index directory:

- An index entry there leads to the upper file.
- A whiteout, the marker that overlayfs uses for a removed file, means
  that the overlay file was removed.

The name of an index entry is the handle that copy up encoded for the
origin, as a hex string.

ovl_lower_fh_to_d() builds the name for this lookup from the bytes that
the caller passed in. But handles with different bytes can decode to the
same inode:

- Overlayfs ignores some flag bits of the handle.
- A lower filesystem can accept a different fid type, extra bytes, or
  generation 0 for any generation.

Such a handle decodes to the origin but misses the index entry or the
whiteout. So the decode returns an overlay inode that has only the lower
file.

While that inode is cached, a path lookup of a copied up file fails with
ESTALE, since the upper file that the lookup finds does not match the
cached inode, which has none.

Reproduced on tmpfs and on ext4 with open_by_handle_at(), after a copy
up and a mount cycle. A handle in which one flag bit, the fid type, the
length or the generation was changed read the old lower data, and path
lookups returned ESTALE.

Fix this by re-encoding the decoded origin and building the index name
from that handle.

CVE-2026-99617.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99617.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow

An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE character device with
major:minor 1:1, so opening it uses the /dev/mem file operations. It
maps one page from offset 0xfffffffffffff000 at user address zero.
The next openat() with a NULL pathname triggers a synchronous external
abort (SEA, ESR 0x96000010) in strncpy_from_user() via do_getname(),
panicking the kernel.

valid_mmap_phys_addr_range() checks the exclusive end by adding the
mapping size to the starting address. For this offset, the sum wraps
to zero and passes the PHYS_MASK test, allowing an out-of-range PFN to
reach remap_pfn_range(). The inclusive-end overflow check in
mmap_mem_prepare() does not catch it because the end is ULONG_MAX.

Reject starting PFNs outside PHYS_MASK and compare the inclusive length
against the remaining physical range without overflowing. This also
allows mappings that end exactly at PHYS_MASK, which the old check
incorrectly rejects.

[catalin.marinas@arm.com: changed the check to look more like __access_ok()]

CVE-2026-99618.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99618.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page

The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target
so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in
the ANA log page.  The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee
that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid
page data.  Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.

CVE-2026-99619.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99619.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: don't drop the gang dependency fence twice

drm_sched_job_add_dependency() drops the fence reference when it fails,
but amdgpu_cs_submit() drops it again, so the scheduled fence of a gang
member loses a reference it still needs.

A GFX+COMPUTE gang waiting for another context, with the
xarray node allocation for the leader's dependency failed through
failslab:

  WARNING: drivers/dma-buf/dma-fence.c:589 at dma_fence_release+0x34d/0x730, CPU#1: amd_uapi_regres/2993
   drm_sched_job_cleanup+0x2c2/0x340 [gpu_sched]
   amdgpu_job_free+0xcb/0x3e0 [amdgpu]
   amdgpu_cs_parser_fini+0x435/0x710 [amdgpu]
   amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0xcd2/0x7a60 [amdgpu]
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f]
  RIP: 0010:dma_fence_signal_timestamp_locked+0x1b8/0x610

(cherry picked from commit 5aa070a83c8378810b906cc8bfc650ce69822a7c)

CVE-2026-99620.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99620.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: don't walk the CS chunks when allocating them failed

amdgpu_cs_pass1() sets p->nchunks before allocating p->chunks, and the
allocation failure path skips resetting it. amdgpu_cs_parser_fini() then
frees the kdata of nchunks chunks from a NULL array. On navi48 with the
chunk array allocation failed through failslab:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f]
  RIP: 0010:amdgpu_cs_parser_fini+0x35d/0x710 [amdgpu]
   amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0xcae/0x7a20 [amdgpu]
   drm_ioctl_kernel+0x180/0x320 [drm]

Set nchunks once the array exists.

(cherry picked from commit 0c828445757b86aaa3ed2638832d76f450022bdf)

CVE-2026-99621.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99621.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: unlock the VM and BO when attaching a KFD BO fails

kfd_mem_attach() locks the page directory and the BO with a drm_exec
transaction on its stack, but leaves through the unwind label without
drm_exec_fini() when locking fails, e.g. when MAP_MEMORY_TO_GPU gets a
signal while the page directory or the BO is busy. Reservations already
acquired then remain locked with their ww_acquire_ctx pointing into the
expired stack frame.

With one thread doing GEM_VA map/unmap on the KFD VM and
another one mapping KFD BOs while getting SIGUSR1 every 20 us:

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in __ww_mutex_lock.constprop.0+0x34f5/0x3da0
   ww_mutex_lock_interruptible+0x2f/0x150
   drm_exec_lock_obj+0x107/0x2d0 [drm_exec]
   kfd_mem_attach+0x4dd/0x1b60 [amdgpu]

and the process ends up in D state.

Finish the transaction before unwinding.

(cherry picked from commit 7b885fa27e4b9fa5cbdc64e66fc35872aee296f5)

CVE-2026-99623.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99623.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Clamp the ATIF backlight curve to its 99 points

amdgpu_atif_query_backlight_caps() stores the firmware's number_of_points
as data_points but copies only the 99 points that luminance_data[] holds.
number_of_points is a u8, so a firmware table that claims more makes the
custom curve code in amdgpu_dm index past the array, and
dm_query_extended_brightness_caps() copy past the end of the
data_points[] buffer it fills

Clamp the count to ATIF_QBTC_MAX_DATA_POINTS and warn, since a table
that claims more is a firmware bug

(cherry picked from commit af8a1c2b7d3de4960e10f94e8ba2fc0ccd168072)

CVE-2026-99624.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99624.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Report MES ring wait timeouts.

Return -ETIMEDOUT when the fence wait before submission expires instead
of reporting success without submitting the packet.

(cherry picked from commit 34341594a87b4a3f28be41e3e70a4787f02b3d9e)

CVE-2026-99625.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99625.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases

drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence reference on success
and failure. Do not release the fence again if
drm_sched_job_add_dependency() fails.

(cherry picked from commit e04f3dfb2071451633e6440a3911a9bb65df9144)

CVE-2026-99626.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99626.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto

[Why]
resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe
is found for a given stream. The current code dereferences this pointer
without a NULL check. This may lead to a possible NULL pointer
dereference.

[How]
Add an explicit NULL check and skip the stream if the OTG master is not
found. This is similar to dcn60_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto().

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.

(cherry picked from commit ffde3d74c1faeeb645b66d02d02fdae3e073941b)

CVE-2026-99627.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99627.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID

gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL
over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. When GFX is in
GFXOFF at that point the update doesn't stick, and with the SPM VMID
programmed on submission again, the job of a process with a reserved
VMID can still run with the SPM writing through VMID 0.

On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM,
a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the
update was called for it:

  $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe)
  RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000

With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15.

(cherry picked from commit 907aebc5578ae09fa5c0e2f0784201295837e60b)

CVE-2026-99629.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99629.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts for navi10_ih

Port this change to navi10_ih.c:
commit afbf7955ff01 ("drm/amdgpu: clear RB_OVERFLOW bit when enabling interrupts")

Setting IH_RB_WPTR to 0 does not clear RB_OVERFLOW if RB_ENABLE is not
set. Pulse WPTR_OVERFLOW_CLEAR after RB_ENABLE (and with
WPTR_OVERFLOW_ENABLE) so overflow is cleared when interrupts are
enabled.

(cherry picked from commit 713fb4ab04f4d2af6120f8eb607c5673b2759b38)

CVE-2026-99631.title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolve ...
CVE-2026-99631.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: check amdgpu_vm_ready() in dma-buf move notify

amdgpu_dma_buf_move_notify() touches the page tables without first
calling amdgpu_vm_ready(). When a process is SIGKILLed, its VM entities
are stopped. Teardown of an imported dma-buf then tries to clear PTEs by
submitting to one of those stopped entities. That eventually hangs the
task.

Commit aa5fc4362fac ("drm/amdgpu: fix task hang from failed job
submission during process kill") added the stopped entity check in
